claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Pack aluminization uses an Al-rich pack to produce an aluminum-enriched surface layer.
Pack aluminization of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will produce a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a physical barrier to oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Reduced oxygen diffusion will minimize deleterious oxidation of the constituent alloying elements.
Suppressing oxidation of the alloying elements will preserve the alloy's mechanical integrity.
After exposure to air at approximately 1000 °C for 100 hours, aluminized specimens will exhibit markedly lower weight gain than untreated specimens.
After oxidation exposure, aluminized specimens will retain room-temperature tensile ductility similar to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
After oxidation exposure, aluminized specimens will retain high-temperature yield strength similar to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr oxidizes rapidly during high-temperature exposure in air.
Rapid high-temperature oxidation of untreated HfNbTaTiZr leads to mechanical-performance degradation.
The proposed benefit is expected around 1000 °C in air under static oxidation conditions and mechanical-test strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
A brittle or excessively thick alumina scale could spall under mechanical stress.
